bullets.title: MU: Massive Q3 Beat + Q4 Guide; $100B in Strategic Customer Agreements Lock In AI Demand
bullets.body: Micron reported F3Q26 revenue of $41.46B (+15% vs $35.9B consensus) and EPS of $25.11 vs $20.86 expected, with non-GAAP gross margin of 84.9% vs 81.7% consensus. F4Q26 guidance of $50B revenue, $31 EPS, and ~86% gross margin all came in ~15-20% above buyside expectations. The company signed 16 strategic customer agreements (SCAs) covering ~20% of DRAM and 33% of NAND volume through 2030, with 14 of 16 carrying ~$100B in cumulative minimum revenue commitments on take-or-pay terms; supply-demand tightness is expected to persist beyond calendar 2027. Stock +13% AH; Citi maintains Buy with $1,200 PT.

bullets.title: AVGO: OpenAI 'Jalapeno' Custom Chip Deal; 50% Cost Savings vs GPUs
bullets.body: Broadcom unveiled its first custom inference chip for OpenAI ('Jalapeno'), offering ~50% cost savings vs typical AI GPUs; shipments expected to exceed 1.3GW soft guide with per-GW silicon content of ~$15/GW vs $11/GW for TPU. AVGO was one of the strongest semi performers on the day on the news, highlighting the broader narrative of hyperscaler diversification away from Nvidia.

bullets.title: GOOGL: AI Talent Drain to Anthropic Accelerates; DJIA Addition and $8.3B Legal Exposure
bullets.body: Google is losing multiple high-profile AI researchers to Anthropic, including Nobel laureate John Jumper (AlphaFold co-creator) and researchers Jonas Adler and Alexander Prtizel; GOOGL fell ~2.45% in premarket on the news. On the positive side, Google will replace VZ in the DJIA effective 6/29. Separately, Sweden's Patent and Market Court postponed its PriceRunner antitrust judgment (seeking ~$8.3B in damages) from 6/26 to 7/1 — procedural only, no inference on outcome.

bullets.title: META: Qualcomm Multi-Generation Data Center CPU Deal; Production H2 2028
bullets.body: Qualcomm and Meta announced a strategic multi-generation collaboration for data center CPUs, with the Qualcomm Dragonfly C1000 planned to power Meta's next-generation server fleet starting H2 2028. This is part of Qualcomm's broader pivot toward non-handset revenue, targeting $15B+ in data center revenue by FY29.

bullets.title: ONON: UBS Reiterates Buy, $85 PT; Run Specialty Weakness Is Strategic, Not Demand
bullets.body: UBS reiterates Buy on On Holding with an $85 PT, dismissing US Run Specialty channel softness as deliberate inventory management ahead of an October innovation cycle featuring new SURREAL superfoam tech (Cloudsurfer 3, Cloudrunner Max). Run Specialty order books are up >25% YoY and UBS forecasts 18/20/29% 5-year CAGRs for sales/EBITDA/EPS with P/E expansion from 18x to 33x FY2 underpinning the target.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: NY & CA AGs Expected to Sue to Block $81B Merger; EU Concessions Offered
bullets.body: Paramount Skydance expects NY and CA attorneys general to jointly sue to block its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on job-loss grounds, with California AG expected to lead. PSKY is prepared to divest its Universal film distribution JV to address EU antitrust concerns, with the EU deadline potentially extended to July 21.

bullets.title: AFRM: +8.1% on Day as Fintech/Non-Bank Lenders Outperform
bullets.body: Affirm surged 8.1% as the fintech/non-bank lender sector rallied broadly (+2.5% for cards/payments), contrasting with asset manager weakness driven by Blackstone's weak Q2 realizations (~40% below consensus at $500M).

bullets.title: BTDR: Citizens Initiates at Market Outperform; HPC Pivot Well Underway
bullets.body: Citizens Financial initiated coverage of Bitdeer at Market Outperform, noting the pivot from Bitcoin mining to high-performance computing is well underway with near-term cash generation support.

bullets.title: SMR/OKLO: Nuclear SMR Stocks Weaken on DOE Loan Commentary
bullets.body: Small modular reactor stocks declined mid-session with SMR -6.0% and OKLO -5.5%. Mizuho noted the DOE's $17.5B nuclear loan commitment has no near-term impact on new utility plant development, dampening sentiment.

bullets.title: CLS: +3.3% as Tech Hardware Names WDC, MRVL, SNDK, CRWV Sell Off 4-8%
bullets.body: Celestica gained 3.3% in Canadian trading while sector peers Western Digital (-7.8%), Marvell (-4.0%), SanDisk (-4.2%), and CoreWeave (-6.1%) all declined meaningfully, consistent with the broader semis/memory weakness during the session ahead of the MU print.

bullets.title: INTC: SambaNova Raising $800M–$1B at $10B Valuation (5x Prior Round in 4 Months)
bullets.body: Intel-backed SambaNova is set to raise $800M–$1B at ~$10B valuation, approximately 5x its prior round from just four months ago. Intel has committed at least $100M (potentially $150M) in SambaNova's February 2026 round; the FTC cleared the Intel-SambaNova transaction in May 2026.

bullets.title: AMZN: Prime Day Sales $8.3B, +5.3% YoY, Beat Forecasts
bullets.body: Amazon Prime Day initial sales came in at $8.3B, +5.3% year-over-year vs. a $7.9B forecast, with strength in electronics, appliances, tools, and home/garden. Amazon is also pursuing warehouse acquisitions in UK and German markets.

bullets.title: SPOT: Jefferies Bull/Bear Lunch July 8; Rates Buy at $600 PT on AI Remixing
bullets.body: Jefferies analyst James Heaney (rated Buy, $600 PT on SPOT) is hosting a NYC bull/bear investor lunch on July 8, focusing on AI remixing adoption, margin implications, and catalysts from Q1 results and Investor Day.

bullets.title: EXPE/ABNB: Travel OTAs Surge; EXPE +9-10%, ABNB at 18-Month Highs
bullets.body: Consumer travel names rallied sharply mid-session with Expedia up ~9-10% and Airbnb hitting 18-month highs, aided by lower oil prices and improving consumer positioning. GLW also gained ~10% on the day.

bullets.title: GOOGL AI Talent Risk: Broader Signal for AI Moat Stocks
bullets.body: Multiple high-profile departures from Google DeepMind to Anthropic — including Nobel laureate John Jumper — represent a meaningful talent-drain risk narrative for GOOGL heading into the second half. The stock was down ~2.45% premarket and underperformed the broader market on the day.
